Research Overview

Compare expanding and five-year rolling training, and post-call CAR horizons ending at Day +5 or +20. Model A uses the common control block, B selects LM inputs in historical temporal validation, and B* uses all eight retained LM inputs.

The outer years were examined in earlier research. The new model fits and feature decisions use only information from earlier calls and mature labels.

Statistical Inference

Pointwise 95% intervals use paired issuer-cluster and two-month-block draws. Intervals condition on the fitted forecasts and remain exploratory.

Partial 2026 has insufficient time blocks. The issuer intervals address repeated issuers and cannot substitute for calendar-time dependence.

Research Insights and Methodology

  • Rolling improved Rank IC in 7, 1 and 7 of 12 cases in 2024, 2025 and partial 2026.
  • The long horizon led on matched calls in 10, 3 and 12 of 12 cases. The partial 2026 comparison has issuer-cluster intervals only.
  • 0 of 48 model-LM issuer intervals exclude zero. B selected no LM inputs in 2 of 24 fits.
  • Prepared-tone change appeared in 15 B fits and answer-hedging change in 12. Raw answer-tone change had negative Rank IC in 12 of 12 test benchmark-horizon cells.
Timing, label maturity and interpretation

Predictions use the original Day 0 mapping and occur after the conservative Day +1 close and before the Day +2 session open. CAR uses close-to-close daily returns. The first return includes overnight repricing after the preceding close. These event results cannot establish executable returns. Short horizons may capture immediate repricing. Longer horizons may capture slower incorporation and other price movement.
